questions.stem:

$$\mathrm{P}(B) = \frac{1}{2} \qquad \mathrm{P}(A|B) = \frac{2}{5} \qquad \mathrm{P}(A \cup B) = \frac{13}{20}$$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find $\mathrm{P}(A \cap B)$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $\mathrm{P}(A \cap B) = \mathrm{P}(A|B) \times \mathrm{P}(B)$
$\mathrm{P}(A \cap B) = \frac{2}{5} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{5}$ M1 A1
M1: for $\frac{2}{5} \times \frac{1}{2}$ or a correct probability product expression and one correct prob. Ans only 2/2

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Draw a Venn diagram to show the events $A$, $B$ and all the associated probabilities.
(3)

B1: for box and $\frac{7}{20}$

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Find
(c) $\mathrm{P}(A)$
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: (c) $\left[\mathrm{P}(A) = \frac{3}{20}+\frac{1}{5}\right] = \frac{7}{20}$ or 0.35. parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) $\mathrm{P}(B|A)$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) $\mathrm{P}(B|A) = \frac{\mathrm{P}(A \cap B)}{\mathrm{P}(A)} = \frac{\frac{1}{5}}{\frac{7}{20}}$ M1: for $\frac{\text{their (a)}}{\text{their (c)}}$ or a correct ratio of probabilities from their diagram. questions.stem:
The table shows the time, to the nearest minute, spent waiting for a taxi by each of 80 people one Sunday afternoon.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline \text{Waiting time (in minutes)} & \text{Frequency}\\ \hline 2\text{–}4 & 15\\ \hline 5\text{–}6 & 9\\ \hline 7 & 6\\ \hline 8 & 24\\ \hline 9\text{–}10 & 14\\ \hline 11\text{–}15 & 12\\ \hline\end{array}$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Write down the upper class boundary for the 2–4 minute interval.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: (a) 4.5. B1: for 4.5 (o.e.) only. NB 1.5~4.5 is B0

parts.label: b
parts.text:
A histogram is drawn to represent these data. The height of the tallest bar is 6 cm.
(b) Calculate the height of the second tallest bar.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) f.d. = 24 is represented as 6cm, so f.d. = 7 is represented as 1.75(cm). M1: for evidence of f/w (at least 3 f.d. found). May be implied by a correct answer. A1: for identifying 9-10 as 2nd highest bar from correct working e.g. 24x = 6$\times$7. A1: for 1.75(cm). Correct answer only 3/3
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Time / Frequency density: 2-4: 5; 5-6: 4.5; 7: 6; 8: 24; 9-10: 7; 11-15: 2.4

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Estimate the number of people with a waiting time between 3.5 minutes and 7 minutes.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: (c) $\frac{1}{3}\times 15 + 9 + \frac{1}{2}\times 6 = 17$ M1: for a correct expression. May interpolate e.g. $\left[24+\frac{1}{2}\times 6 - \frac{2}{3}\times 15\right]$ or (27−10). A1: for 17

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) Use linear interpolation to estimate the median, the lower quartile and the upper quartile of the waiting times.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) Median $= 7.5+\frac{40-30}{24}\times 1 = 7.91666\ldots$ awrt 7.92 or 7.93(75). M1 A1
$Q_1 = 4.5+\frac{20-15}{9}\times 2 = 5.6111111\ldots$ awrt 5.61 or 5.66(666…). A1
$Q_3 = 8.5+\frac{60-54}{14}\times 2 = 9.357142\ldots$ awrt 9.36 or 9.46(4285…). A1
M1: for one correct fraction in an expression for $Q_1$, $Q_2$ or $Q_3$. 1st A1 for $Q_2$ awrt 7.92 (or 7.94 if (n+1) used – look for 40.5 instead of 40). 2nd A1 for $Q_1$ awrt 5.61 (or 5.67 if (n+1) used – look for 20.25 instead of 20). 3rd A1 for $Q_3$ awrt 9.36 (or 9.46 if (n+1) used – look for 60.75 instead of 60). NB watch out for working down e.g. $8.5-\frac{14}{24}\times 1$ for $Q_2$

parts.label: e
parts.text:
(e) Describe the skewness of these data, giving a reason for your answer.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(e) $Q_3 - Q_2 (=1.4\text{ or }1.5) < Q_2 - Q_1 (=2.3)$ or (Mean) < Median < Mode. B1ft: for a correct comparison of their quartiles e.g. $Q_2$ closer to $Q_3$ or using at least two of Mean < Median < Mode (must state mean or mode if using this method). N.B. Mean = 7.71875, mode = 8.
Therefore negative skew. dB1cao: dependent on 1st B1 being awarded for negative skew only (no ft)

questions.stem: The time taken, in minutes, by children to complete a mathematical puzzle is assumed to be normally distributed with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$. The puzzle can be completed in less than 24 minutes by 80% of the children. For 5% of the children it takes more than 28 minutes to complete the puzzle.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show this information on the Normal curve below.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: (a) 24 and 28 labelled on the horizontal axis above the mean in the correct order. B1: 24 and 28 (above the mean). B1: for 0.80 and 0.05 (clearly indicated), must be clear, correct labelling of probabilities associated with correct area

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Write down the percentage of children who take between 24 minutes and 28 minutes to complete the puzzle.
(1)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) (i) Find two equations in $\mu$ and $\sigma$.
(ii) Hence find, to 3 significant figures, the value of $\mu$ and the value of $\sigma$.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c)(i) $\frac{(28-\mu)}{\sigma}=1.64(49)$ or $\frac{(24-\mu)}{\sigma}=0.84(16)$ M1: for $\frac{\pm(28-\mu)}{\sigma}=z_1$ or $\frac{\pm(24-\mu)}{\sigma}=z_2$ where $|z_1|>1.5$ and $|z_2|<1$. Condone $z_2=0.8$
0.8416 and 1.6449 seen B1: for both values 0.8416 and 1.6449 or better seen. Calc: 0.8416212.., 1.644853..
$\mu = 28-1.64(49)\sigma$, $\mu = 24-0.84(16)\sigma$ A1, A1: 1st A1 for $\mu=28-1.64(49)\sigma$ or any correct arrangement (allow 1.64~1.65 inclusive). 2nd A1 for $\mu=24-0.84(16)\sigma$ or any correct arrangement (allow 0.84 or better)
(ii) $24-0.8416\sigma = 28-1.6449\sigma$ (eliminating $\mu$ or $\sigma$) M1: for an attempt to solve simultaneous equations by eliminating $\mu$ or $\sigma$
$\sigma = 4.9794597\ldots$ awrt 4.98 A1
$\mu = 19.809286\ldots$ awrt 19.8 A1
SC: For use of 0.84 and 1.64 giving $\sigma=5$ and $\mu=$ awrt 19.8 score M1B0A1A1M1A1A1, or 0.84 and 1.65 giving $\sigma=$ awrt 4.94 and $\mu=$ awrt 19.9 score M1B0A1A1M1A1A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- 3rd A1 for **awrt** 4.98 (Condone $\sigma = 5$ or awrt 5.0 if B0 scored)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
A child is selected at random.
(d) Find the probability that the child takes less than 12 minutes to complete the puzzle.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) $z=\frac{(12-'19.8...')}{'4.97...'}$ M1: for standardising with 12, their $\mu$ and $\sigma$ provided $\sigma>0$. If $\sigma<0$ from their equations in (c) allow M1 if they use $|\sigma|$

$1-0.9418 = 0.0582$ awrt 0.06 A1: for awrt 0.06 from correct working

questions.stem:
In a large company,

78% of employees are car owners,
30% of these car owners are also bike owners,
85% of those who are not car owners are bike owners.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Draw a tree diagram to represent this information.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme: (a) Tree diagram: 0.78 car owner, 0.30 bike owner (giving $\frac{117}{500}$), (0.70) not bike owner (giving $\frac{273}{500}$); (0.22) not car owner, 0.85 bike owner (giving $\frac{187}{1000}$), (0.15) not bike owner (giving $\frac{33}{1000}$). B1: for a (2+4) tree with 6 branches. B1: for 0.78 with label. B1: for 0.30 and 0.85 with label

parts.label: b
parts.text:
An employee is selected at random.
(b) Find the probability that the employee is a car owner or a bike owner but not both.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: (b) $\mathrm{P}(\text{car or bike but not both}) = 0.78\times 0.70 + 0.22\times 0.85 = 0.733$ M1: for correct expression of follow through their correct tree branches. A1: for 0.733 or exact equivalent e.g. $\frac{733}{1000}$ and allow 73.3%

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Another employee is selected at random.
Given that this employee is a bike owner,
(c) find the probability that the employee is a car owner.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $\left[\mathrm{P}(\text{car}|\text{bike})\right] = \frac{\mathrm{P}(\text{car}\cap\text{bike})}{\mathrm{P}(\text{bike})} = \frac{0.78\times 0.30}{0.78\times 0.30+0.22\times 0.85} = 0.555819\ldots$
M1: for a correct expression correct ft or correct formula and $\frac{1\text{ product}}{\text{sum of 2 products}}$ with at least 2 products correct or correct ft. Ratio must be smaller than 1
1st A1: for finding the denominator correctly. Fully correct expression or $= 0.421$ (oe)
awrt 0.556 2nd A1: for awrt 0.556 or exact equivalent e.g. $\frac{234}{421}$ and allow 55.6%

parts.label: d
parts.text:
Two employees are selected at random.
(d) Find the probability that only one of them is a bike owner.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) $\mathrm{P}(\text{bike}) = 0.78\times 0.30+0.22\times 0.85 = 0.421$, $\mathrm{P}(\text{not bike}) = 1-0.421$ M1: for their $\mathrm{P}(\text{bike})\times(1-\mathrm{P}(\text{bike}))$
$0.421\times 0.579+0.579\times 0.421$ dM1: for $\times 2$
$= 0.487518$ awrt 0.488 A1: for awrt 0.488
